title: Things are more malleable than they seem
author: Mark Goodrich
summary: Mark Goodrich introduces his first 'bee', a personal obsession that is hard to argue away: that schools too easily accept that some things cannot be changed. The idea was sparked by an interview in which Katharine Birbalsingh, famously a believer in changing almost anything in a school, justified low numbers of girls taking physics at Michaela by pointing to hard maths. He notes the inconsistency, since the same leader would never accept 'our kids won't line up in silence' or 'our kids won't behave in lessons'. His own blind spot was handwriting, which he thought would always be poor for some children until a visit to Stanley Road Primary showed book after book of legible writing from ordinary pupils. He ends with a caution that change is hard and demands focus and follow-through, but hard is not impossible, and teachers should find out who has already done what they want to do.
points: Schools reveal their assumptions in the phrase 'our kids won't', which treats some outcomes as fixed while treating others, like behaviour, as changeable.
Even a leader known for high expectations can hold a blind spot, as Birbalsingh did with girls and physics, so the habit is common rather than a failing of weak schools.
Seeing a school that actually achieves the outcome, as Goodrich did with handwriting at Stanley Road Primary, is what dissolves the belief that it cannot be done.
Changing something is hard and needs focus and follow-through, so the claim is that it is possible, not that it is easy.
The practical step is to name what you think cannot change in your school and find who has changed it elsewhere.
quotes: One that has been buzzing in my head for a few years is that schools too easily accept that some things can’t be changed.
It was revealing what we treat as an unchanging fact of life that we can’t do much about and what we treat as susceptible to being changed.
We all have blind spots of things that we just accept as the way things are. One of mine was handwriting.
The children at the school weren’t any different to the children I was teaching; the school just had an incredible focus on making sure all children could write neatly and legibly.
These things can be changed and schools have shown that they can be.

However, hard is not impossible and we can do hard things. If there is something you feel can’t be changed in school but you really want to, think long and hard about what you could try and who and where you could learn from.
